details.description: This is a "latest" alias for Z.ai's (Zhipu AI) GLM series; it currently resolves to GLM-5.3, Z.ai's flagship open-weight large language model. GLM-5.3 is built for complex software engineering, long-horizon agentic workflows and cybersecurity vulnerability research, and it always reasons, at a configurable low, high or max effort level; disabling reasoning is not supported. Z.ai states GLM-5.3 shares the same base model as GLM-5.2, with all of its gains coming from post-training, and reports a 50% improvement in coding performance over GLM-5.2 on its internal benchmarks. Because this id tracks Z.ai's latest GLM release, the specific model it points to can change over time.
advantages: Z.ai reports 50% better coding performance than GLM-5.2 on its internal benchmarks (Z.ai docs).
Scores 84.5 on CyberGym, a cybersecurity vulnerability-discovery benchmark, up from GLM-5.2's 77.2, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 78.1 on the FrontierSWE coding benchmark, up from 67.5 for GLM-5.2, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 28.3 on Terminal Bench 3.0, versus 4.6 for GLM-5.2, per its Hugging Face model card.
Supports three configurable reasoning effort levels (low, high, max) for coding and agentic tasks (Z.ai docs).
disadvantages: Text-only input and output, with no image, audio or video support (Z.ai docs).
Documented language support is limited to English and Chinese (Hugging Face model card).
Always reasons before responding; disabling reasoning is not supported, per Z.ai's documentation.
As a "latest" alias, the underlying model version can change without this id changing, per Mistral's documentation.
use_cases: Complex software engineering and long-horizon coding-agent workflows
Cybersecurity vulnerability discovery and exploit research

sources.title: Model lifecycle policy - Mistral AI Documentation

notes: Mistral's dedicated model page (docs.mistral.ai/models/zai-glm-5-3) lists three names for the same model entry: `zai-glm-5-3`, `zai-glm-5`, and `zai-glm-latest` — confirming `zai-glm-latest` currently points to GLM-5.3, the same model as the `zai-glm-5-3` target in this batch. Mistral's model-lifecycle page documents `-latest` generally as an alias for the newest version, which can move to a different underlying model over time. I described this entry as an alias rather than duplicating a from-scratch profile, since the two targets are the same model today. The Hugging Face model card's '300,000 tokens' figure is not a general usable-context claim: it is a footnote on the HLE w/ Tools score giving the context length used specifically for that one evaluation, so it does not actually conflict with the 1M context window Z.ai's docs, Mistral's docs and the catalog facts all give; kept the catalog's 1,048,576 figure.
